turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to see me?
turns.patient_response:
Well, hello doctor. I came in because... well, at church, I keep doing these odd things. We have a potluck every Sunday down in the basement. Pastor Thomas always says a real long prayer before we can eat, and my knees just ache with all that standing. I used to get my good shoes from Sears, but they closed the Sears down by the mall, you know. It's a crying shame, they always had the best catalogs. I used to look at those catalogs for hours when I was a girl... 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, the church food. I was standing right by the potluck table, and I just... I held the serving spoon up in the air and didn't move. Just froze right there with the spoon up. And then later I was folding the exact same stack of napkins over and over again. Folks were just standing in line waiting on me to move. They were those nice thick napkins, not the cheap thin ones that tear when you wipe your mouth. I always tell Mary to buy the thick ones for the church... but yes, folks were just waiting on me, and I couldn't stop folding them.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and derailment, wandering off-topic to discuss Sears, shoes, and catalogs, and losing her train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes abnormal motor behaviors, including freezing in place with a serving spoon (posturing/catalepsy) and repetitively folding the same napkins (stereotypy).

turns.doctor_question: When you froze with the spoon and kept folding the napkins, what was going through your mind?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I... I don't really know. I don't think much of anything was going through my mind, to be honest. It was just sort of quiet in my head. I was just holding that big serving spoon. It’s one of the heavy silver ones we keep in the locked cabinet. Pastor Thomas says we have to keep the good silver locked up now because anyone can just wander right in off the street during service. We had a fellow come in last winter during a bad freeze, just shivering to the bone, wearing a jacket that was entirely too thin for December. I felt so awful for him, I tried to get him a bowl of Mary's chili to warm him up. Mary makes a decent chili, but Lord, she puts way too many onions in it. It gives me the most terrible heartburn. I always have to chew on those little pink chalky tablets after I eat her cooking. 

But... what were you asking me? Oh, about my mind. No, I wasn't thinking about a single thing. It was just blank.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and derailment, wandering far off-topic from the spoon to a church cabinet, a homeless man, chili, and heartburn before finally returning to the doctor's question.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from these freezing moments, how has your mood been lately—have you been feeling down or depressed?
turns.patient_response:
Well, my mood? No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling depressed. I feel just fine, really. I mean, I get up every morning and I make my coffee. I have to use the decaf now because the regular kind makes my heart flutter like a little bird in a cage. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she drinks three cups of regular coffee every morning. I don't know how she does it at her age. She's 82, you know, and still drives herself to the grocery store. Though I wouldn't want to be on the road when she's driving, she can barely see over the steering wheel! She has this big old Buick that her husband left her when he passed. He was a nice man, Mr. Higgins. Always kept his lawn looking so neat. Not like the folks across the street who let the dandelions just take over the whole yard. Dandelions are just terrible for my allergies... 

But no, I'm not depressed at all. Just fine.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's response demonstrates tangentiality, wandering from the topic of their mood to coffee, a neighbor, driving, lawns, and allergies.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling depressed, stating multiple times that they feel 'just fine'.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices, whispering, or other sounds when no one was around?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? Oh, no. No, I don't hear anything like that. It gets mighty quiet in my house since I live by myself. Well, I say quiet, but old houses always make their own noises, don't they? The floorboards creak, and sometimes the wind whistles through the crack in the kitchen window. I asked Mr. Henderson, my landlord, to fix it, oh, it must have been three months ago now. He said he'd send someone over, but you know how that goes. You just can't rely on folks these days to do what they say. 

It’s just like the boy who delivers my newspaper. Half the time he throws it right into my rosebushes. I try to tell him to just leave it on the porch step, but he rides by so fast on that bicycle. It’s one of those bright red ones with the thick tires. My grandson wanted a bicycle just like that for his birthday, but Lord, they are just terribly expensive now. I went to the store to look at the prices and nearly fell over. Everything is so high. A loaf of bread costs near as much as a whole meal used to... 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, whispering. No, no whispering or voices, just the wind and the house creaking.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, wandering through loosely connected topics like her landlord, the newspaper boy, bicycles, and grocery prices before finally returning to the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or whispering, stating she only hears normal house noises like the wind and creaking floorboards.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions or had any new physical illnesses recently?
turns.patient_response:
Medical conditions? Well, no, I haven't been told I have any new illnesses or anything like that. My health has been pretty steady, thank the Lord. Though my knees do ache when it rains, but that's just getting older, isn't it? Dr. Evans, my regular doctor, he always checks my blood pressure and says I'm doing fine for my age. I've been going to him for... oh, it must be fifteen years now. His office used to be right down on Elm Street, right next to that little bakery that made the most wonderful cherry danishes. Oh, I used to treat myself to one every time I had an appointment. But then the bakery closed down when the owners moved to Florida. Florida is just too hot for me. My sister went down there for a vacation once and she said the humidity was like walking through a bowl of hot soup. She brought me back a snow globe with a flamingo in it, though. It's sitting right on my mantelpiece next to the picture of my grandson in his little baseball uniform... 

But no, no new medical conditions or anything. I'm just fine.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's response demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from their doctor to a bakery, Florida, a snow globe, and their grandson before finally returning to the question.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt like people were watching you, following you, or plotting against you?
turns.patient_response:
Watching me? Oh heavens, no. Nobody's following me or plotting anything. Well, I suppose Doris down the street is always peeking through her blinds when I go out to check the mail, but she's just a busybody. She has those awful heavy velvet drapes, you know the kind? They must collect just a terrible amount of dust. I don't know how she breathes in that house. I always like to keep my windows open to let the fresh air in when it gets warm. Spring cleaning is just so important. When I was a little girl, I used to help my mother beat the rugs out on the clothesline. We had this big wooden paddle, and oh, the dust that would fly out! You just don't see people doing that anymore. Everyone has those heavy vacuum cleaners now. I have one, but the cord always gets tangled around the legs of my coffee table. It's a nice table, though, solid oak. My husband bought it for me oh, it must be forty years ago now... 

But anyway, what was it you asked? Oh, right, plotting against me. No, no, nothing like that. Just Doris being nosy.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, wandering from a neighbor's drapes to spring cleaning, beating rugs, and a coffee table before finally returning to the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies feeling watched, followed, or plotted against, stating 'Nobody's following me or plotting anything.'

turns.doctor_question: About how long have you been experiencing these freezing spells?
turns.patient_response:
Freezing spells? You mean when I just stop and get stuck, and folks say my talking gets all mixed up and hard to follow? Well, I suppose that’s been going on for about six months now. 

Six months... yes, because that was right around when the weather started turning cold. I remember I was trying to get my heavy winter coats out of the cedar closet. I love the smell of cedar, don't you? It keeps the moths away just beautifully. My grandmother had a whole chest made of solid cedar. She kept all her beautiful hand-stitched quilts in there. She made one out of my grandfather's old flannel shirts after he passed. It had the most beautiful blue and red squares. I tried quilting once, but my eyes just aren't good enough for all that tiny stitching anymore. Threading the needle takes me half the morning! I bought one of those little wire threader gadgets from the sewing shop downtown, but I misplaced it almost the minute I got it home. It's probably under the sofa cushion with all the loose change and peppermint wrappers. I always keep a peppermint in my pocket for a dry throat... 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the freezing up and the odd way I've been acting. Yes, it's been about six months since people started noticing that.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient notes that others say their talking gets 'mixed up and hard to follow,' and they actively demonstrate tangential speech by drifting from the topic of freezing spells to cedar closets, quilts, and peppermints before losing their train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient confirms experiencing 'freezing spells' where they 'just stop and get stuck,' which is indicative of cataleptic or stuporous behavior.
